51547885.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to His-tagged full length human CCN2 CT domain assessed as dissociation constant by isothermal titration calorimetry assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: Isothermal Titration Calorimetry. ITC assays were carried out using a MicroCal PEAQ-ITC (Malvern Instruments Ltd) in PBS buffer with a pH of 7.4, and the temperature was maintained at 37 °C. In all experiments, either K2 or OK2 was placed in the syringe, and the CCN2-CT (RPA010Hu01, Cloud-Clone Corporation, Wuhan, China) protein with His Tag was added to the sample cell. The obtained data were analyzed using MicroCal PEAQ-ITC Analysis Software (Malvern Instruments Ltd). The heats of dilution were evaluated using the final injections of each individual titration and were subsequently subtracted before data analysis.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption - ITC profiles: Representative ITC profiles of peptides K2 and OK2 binding to CCN2-CT.
original_paragraph.Figure 4E - ITC thermograms and binding: K2 to CCN2-CT Kd = 3.9 ± 0.7 μM OK2 to CCN2-CT Kd = 3.1 ± 0.6 μM
original_paragraph.Results section - Binding affinity measu: Finally, the binding affinity of peptides K2 and OK2 to the CCN2-CT was measured in an isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) assay. As shown in Figure 4E, K2 and OK2 exhibited moderate affinity toward CCN2-CT, indicating that K2 and OK2 could directly bind CCN2-CT. Consistently, the cyclic peptide OK2 has a binding affinity similar to that of K2 (Figure 4E).
